# Can consistency regularization reduce DPO answer-order bias?

2026-11-26 | Anicca Research

**TL;DR.** We ran 48 actual optimizer steps and reloaded six adapters. DPO's raw order gap was 0.2796; DPO plus consistency 0.0807, a relative reduction of 71.1%. AUROC was 0.6443 versus 0.5996; no production promotion.

![cover](/assets/research/manager-execution-04-consistency-2026-11-26-cover.svg)

Cover: actual UCI test, 128 sessions, 23 positive.

## The problem
Run03 DPO improved descriptive ranking but produced a large difference when answer options were swapped. We tested a consistency penalty inspired by prior consistency training and permutation-bias work. This is for ML engineers familiar with LoRA and classification.

## How we did it
1. Reused SmolLM2-135M and UCI Online Shoppers (CC BY 4.0), train64 (12 positive), calibration64 (10 positive), test128 (23 positive), disjoint from our own previous test slices.
2. Weighted SFT, DPO and DPO plus consistency, seeds42/43, 8 steps each, rank4 alpha8 q/v, batch8, AdamW 3e-4. DPO beta .1; lambda5 fixed before execution, not formally preregistered. The added loss is 5*(p_AB-p_BA)^2, with semantic purchase probabilities.
3. All six saved adapters were reloaded and calibrated predictions checked. All models including logistic used the same calibration slice; both answer orders were averaged for neural predictions.
4. Recomputed AUROC and Brier independently; 2,000 paired stratified bootstrap draws per seed compare DPO plus consistency vs DPO. Intervals condition on fixed predictions and are unadjusted.

![pipeline](/assets/research/manager-execution-04-consistency-2026-11-26-pipeline.svg)

Figure 1. Matched Run04 pipeline, same 128 test sessions for all methods.

## Results

| Model | AUROC | Raw order gap |
|---|---:|---:|
| Logistic | 0.6075 | N/A |
| DPO | 0.6443 | 0.2796 |
| DPO + consistency | 0.5996 | 0.0807 |
| Weighted SFT | 0.5983 | 0.0885 |
| Base | 0.5851 | 0.2058 |
| Prior | 0.5000 | N/A |

![chart](/assets/research/manager-execution-04-consistency-2026-11-26-chart.svg)

Figure 2. Actual Run04 AUROC and raw option-order gap, means across two seeds for trained variants. [Code and receipt](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca/pull/9518). Raw gap is the mean absolute difference in semantic probabilities when options are swapped, before calibration.

## Trade-offs and unverified items
The consistency objective lowers order sensitivity but can reduce discrimination. A constant prediction also has zero gap. Averaging both semantic probabilities makes binary permutation invariance exact by construction, but requires two evaluations and does not guarantee accuracy. We chose a small CPU experiment, only 23 positive test labels and two seeds, not a fully converged comparison. Team-wide and pretraining overlap unknown. No official external benchmark, prospective prediction, causal effects or human benefit established. No promotion.

## Reproduce or contribute
Open [the draft PR with weights, code, audit and predictions](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca/pull/9518) and test matched larger budgets, more seeds, and paraphrase robustness.
